title: Runner resume support and branch collision handling
problem: If any stage fails after a 15-minute run, the entire runner must restart from stage 1. Stages 2-3 redo expensive Claude calls, and stage 4 fails because the branch already exists. There is no way to resume from where it stopped.
description: Add resume-from capability to the orchestrator and make the executor handle existing branches: (1) run.py accepts --resume-from <stage_name> flag that skips earlier stages and picks up from the specified stage using existing artifacts, (2) run.py validates that prerequisite artifacts exist before resuming (e.g. resuming from stage 4 requires plans/<uuid>.json), (3) executor.py detects if branch runner/<uuid> already exists and checks it out instead of failing, (4) on runner failure, run.py prints the exact resume command to rerun from the failed stage.
scope: Modified: runner/run.py (--resume-from flag, artifact validation, resume command on failure). Modified: runner/executor.py (existing branch detection and checkout). No new files.
context: Stages are: validate_intake, auto_refine, auto_plan, executor, auto_harden, approval. Artifact paths are all UUID-derived and predictable. The executor currently does git checkout -b runner/<uuid> which fails if the branch exists. Resume should checkout the existing branch instead.
